findings.title: Hardcoded port 9223 causes port collision
findings.explanation: Every new Claude agent gets hardcoded port 9223. If multiple agents spawn on the same host they will collide on that port and the second one will fail to bind, making the daemon crash or become unreachable.
findings.fix: Use findFreePort() to allocate a unique VS Code debug port, not just the PTY port.

findings.title: Race: lock released before seat-map flushed to disk
findings.explanation: releaseLock() is called immediately after the write but before fs.fsync/sync. If the node process crashes or the OS buffers the write, another spawner can read a half-written JSON and parse it, corrupting state or throwing.
findings.fix: Call fs.fdatasyncSync(fd) on the seat-map file descriptor before releaseLock().

findings.title: PTY port scan starts below already-used base
findings.explanation: seat-map already contains pty_port 9301 and 9302, so the scan restarts at 9300 and will waste cycles testing 9300/9301 before finding 9303. No crash, just slower spawn.
findings.fix: Initialize maxPtyPort with Math.max(9300, ...existing ports).

findings.title: Regex can false-match commented code
findings.explanation: If send-pt-welcome.js contains the key inside a comment or string literal the regex will still extract it, but it will be the wrong value. NOT A BUG because the code will simply fall back to env vars and fail fast with a clear message.
findings.fix: Parse as AST or require() the module instead of regex.

findings.title: Missing file lock handling in spawnClaude
findings.code: try { console.log('[CITY-SPAWN] Acquiring structural lock on seat-map...'); acquireLock(); ... } catch (err) { releaseLock(); console.error('[CITY-SPAWN] Failed to spawn Claude agent:', err); process.exit(1); }
findings.explanation: The code attempts to acquire a file lock using acquireLock() before spawning a new Claude agent. However, if acquireLock() fails due to a timeout or file lock conflict, the catch block only logs the error and exits the process. It does not handle the failure gracefully, potentially leaving the seat-map.json file locked and preventing other processes from accessing it.
findings.fix: Add proper error handling in the catch block to ensure the lock is released and the process exits cleanly. Consider retrying the lock acquisition or implementing a timeout mechanism to prevent deadlocks. For example, you could use a loop with a timeout and a retry mechanism, and ensure releaseLock() is called regardless of success or failure.

findings.title: Lock file race condition
findings.explanation: The lock file creation using 'wx' flag might not prevent race conditions if multiple instances of the script are run simultaneously. findings.fix: Implement a proper lock mechanism that checks the timestamp or owner of the lock file and ensures only the correct process can hold the lock.

findings.title: Race condition in lock acquisition
findings.explanation: The busy-wait loop with process.pid in lock file creates a race condition. If the process crashes, the lock file remains, blocking all future operations. Also, no PID validation is done, so a terminated process's lock can never be cleared.
findings.fix: Use proper advisory file locking (fs2) or a library like proper-lockfile. Add PID validation and stale lock detection with timeout.

findings.title: Port collision in seat assignment
findings.explanation: maxPtyPort is derived from existing seats, but if multiple spawnClaude() processes run simultaneously, they could both calculate the same maxPtyPort and race to bind the same port.
findings.fix: Move the port allocation inside the critical section (after lock is acquired).

findings.title: Stack overflow in port finder
findings.explanation: The recursive findFreePort() call without a base case could theoretically cause a stack overflow if thousands of ports are in use.
findings.fix: Make it iterative or add a maximum port limit with proper error handling.

findings.title: Hardcoded file path
findings.explanation: Assumes send-pt-welcome.js exists in the parent directory. Will throw an error if the file is missing.
findings.fix: Check if file exists before reading, or make the key source configurable.

findings.title: No error handling for JSON parse
findings.explanation: If seat-map.json is malformed or empty, JSON.parse() will throw an uncaught error, leaving the lock file held.
findings.fix: Wrap in try/catch and handle JSON parse errors explicitly.

findings.title: Potential file descriptor leak
findings.code: const out = fs.openSync(logFile, 'a'); const err = fs.openSync(logFile, 'a');
findings.explanation: File descriptors for log files are never closed, which could lead to resource exhaustion over time.
findings.fix: Close the file descriptors after spawning the child process or use a logging library that handles this.

findings.title: Inadequate lock release on error
findings.explanation: If an error occurs after acquiring the lock but before the try block (e.g., in JSON.parse), the lock will not be released, causing deadlock.
findings.fix: Use a finally block or a try/finally pattern to ensure the lock is always released.
